hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try an easier radical: $\sqrt{12} = \sqrt{4}\sqrt{3} = 2\sqrt{3}$. Pull out the largest perfect square you can find; the rest stays under the root.

learningObjective: Simplify a radical by extracting a perfect-square factor.
explanation: Split $50$ into a perfect square times the rest: $50 = 25 \times 2$.
Choice A leaves the $25$ inside and outside at once — the square root of $25$ is $5$, not $25$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check with a decimal
steps: Evaluate the choices: A is about $35.4$, B is about $7.07$ ✓, C is about $4.47$, D is about $22.4$.
A quick decimal estimate is a reliable check on any radical-simplification question, and it needs no rules at all.
